note: The BUDGET law of the `evaluate` capability. `🛑️preview-cancel.json` says what an explicit gesture does to work in flight; this says how a long operator's evaluation is CUT into interactive steps in the first place, so that there is a boundary for the gesture — and for a liveness watchdog — to land on at all. Language-agnostic: an implementation in any language must fold these envelopes and answer the same outcomes, the same published status and the same continuation.

laws.oneRequestOneStep: An `evaluate` request is answered within the requester's own wall allowance, ALWAYS. An operator that cannot finish inside it answers `done: false` with its progress; the chain re-emits the IDENTICAL request and the extension resumes the job it parked under the same `nodeHash`. This is the same resumption mechanism budgeted `tessellate` uses — no timers, no parked futures, because a plugin has nowhere to hold one.
laws.unbudgetedOperatorsAreUnchanged: An operator with no sub-structure completes inside the first round trip and its envelope is indistinguishable in latency from the one-shot call it replaces. Only an operator that offers a resumable job can ever answer `done: false`.
laws.progressIsMonotone: `unitsDone` never decreases across the round trips of one evaluation. `unitsTotal` is the plan known so far and may be revised UPWARD exactly once, when a stage that could only be planned after an earlier one ran finally reports its size.
laws.workingSeedsNothing: A working envelope seeds no node cache entry. Seeding a partial evaluation would publish a half-built solid as if it were the answer.
laws.workingIsInFlight: While an evaluation is working, the published status reports `inFlight >= 1`, a non-idle phase and a ratio below 1 — even though NO tessellation has been admitted. A preview that reports `idle` while its kernel is busy is the defect this fixture exists to forbid.
laws.cancelledOwesNothing: A cancelled envelope seeds nothing and arms nothing: the gesture that produced it already quiesced every latch, and arming here would restart the chain the user stopped.
laws.completeSeedsTheOutput: A complete envelope's `outputJson` is exactly the out dictionary the unbudgeted evaluation would have produced — a stepped answer and a one-shot answer are indistinguishable downstream, including the `{"error": …}` body a refused evaluation carries.
laws.anUnknownPhaseIsComputing: A phase tag the surface's vocabulary does not know reads as `computing`, never as `idle`: the envelope that carried it said the job is still working.
laws.aBareDictionaryIsAFinishedEvaluation: A response body that is not an envelope at all is read as a finished evaluation whose output IS that body. It is the only reading that cannot lose an answer.
laws.theBudgetKeepsTheWorkerAlive: The wall allowance is chosen below the host's shard liveness window, not merely below its termination threshold: a guest turn that never yields blocks the worker's event loop and its progress ticker with it, so a long turn and a dead worker are indistinguishable to the host. Returning between steps is what makes them distinguishable.

rows.why: The headline case: a boolean that spent its wall allowance inside the validation stage.
A future operator's own vocabulary must never be published as `idle`.
The terminal case: the job finished inside this round trip.
The error body travels inside the output exactly as an unbudgeted refusal always did.
The gesture already stopped the chain; this answer only observes it.
An answer that predates the envelope contract must still be an answer, never a lost one.

steppedOperator.why: The one operator family measured long enough to trip the host's 16 s shard watchdog inside a single turn: `🍩️sphere-cut-with-torus` costs 4.5 s of exact boolean natively (1.5 s of it stitching, 3.0 s validating) and over 16 s in the served wasm.
steppedOperator.steppedEqualsOneShot: Driving the job one unit at a time must produce the SAME out dictionary as the one-shot evaluation of the same input. The stepped path IS the algorithm; there is no second implementation to drift from.
steppedOperator.cancelMidWay: Cancelling between steps terminates the job with phase `cancelled`; a job that already produced its output is never retired by a later cancel.
